components.gap: The composite allocation to Carnap 1950 is incomplete because its listed subcomponents N-x-008-S01-PRESENTATION, -PROOF and -BRIDGE are each partial (gaps on those entries). The 1950 source is kept separate from Zabell, the 1952 Continuum and the 1962 edition (handbook/parts/p15/inductive-logic-and-confirmation-w02b-p15-029.tex:32-33; handbook/parts/p15/carnap-logical-probability-and-induction.tex:559-566), so no hybrid replacement holds.

Carnap 1950 presentation not complete on the route: (a) ch. I secs. 1-6 (requirements for an explicatum, classificatory/comparative/quantitative concepts and their use as explicata, formalization and interpretation) and ch. II secs. 8-13 (semantical concepts of confirmation, the logical nature of the two probability concepts, psychologism in deductive and inductive logic, probability as a logical relation) appear only as the summary at handbook/parts/p15/carnap-logical-probability-and-induction.tex:5-37; (b) the ch. III deductive-logic prerequisites (secs. 14-40: rules of formation and truth, theorems on state descriptions and ranges, L-concepts, propositional, general-sentence, replacement and identity theorems, Q-normal form, Q-numbers, simple laws and simple laws of conditional form, the mathematical definitions of sec. 40) are given only where used (secs. 15A, 18, 25-27, 31-34, T20-11, D40-3, T40-12/13/21/32); (c) secs. 43-44 (possibility of exact rules of induction, relation of deductive and inductive logic, methodological problems and inductive inferences) are not presented. Further, the 110I variety-of-instances demonstration (Carnap refers it to his 1945 paper), the comparative vindication of c* and the quantitative-language confirmation function are absent (see blocked items).
